messages:
Eleni (Product): Quick note from customer interviews: people expect the small contextual docs card (the inline ? icon) to land them exactly on the control docs, not the top of the docs page. Several complained that search is a dead end.

Ravi (Design): Agreed. The card currently links to `/docs/console` or to page-level anchors that change when we edit copy. UX suggestion: make the inline card open a modal preview with a one-sentence excerpt and a stable 'open in docs' link.

Kendrick (Docs): Root cause: our heading-derived anchors are brittle. When writers reword a heading the slug changes. We should introduce explicit anchor IDs in markdown like `### Autoscaling {#autoscaling}` and publish a lightweight redirect map.

Sam (DevEx): Implementation ideas: 1) docs add explicit `id` tokens for linkable headings; 2) docs build emits a manifest `/static/anchor-manifest.json` mapping page->anchors; 3) console reads manifest at build-time to verify links and at runtime to resolve previews.

Nina (Support): If we supply a manifest and canonical link examples, I can update our canned responses. Also please include a short human-readable label for each anchor so support can copy it into replies.

A11yBot: Accessibility reminder: when opening a modal preview, ensure focus trap, role="dialog", and announce the destination. For deep-links that jump the page, use `tabindex="-1"` + `.focus()` and honor `prefers-reduced-motion` for the scroll.

Eleni (Product): Good call. Also we need a canonical naming policy so writers don't accidentally create duplicates. Recommendation: kebab-case, avoid punctuation, max 4 words, and begin with the noun (e.g., `dedicated-capacity`).

Kendrick (Docs): I'll add that to the contributor guide and enable a CI linter that warns when a referenced anchor is missing or when a heading lacks an explicit id. We can also emit a deprecation header when an anchor is renamed for a little while.

Ravi (Design): UX detail: when following an in-product deep link, offset the scroll by the nav height + 12px and animate unless `prefers-reduced-motion` is set. Also make the preview modal show a tiny link icon to open docs in a new tab.

Sam (DevEx): I'll prototype the manifest and add a console-side unit that cross-checks the link targets during CI deploy. If an anchor disappears, fail the deploy and surface who last edited the docs heading in the error.

Nina (Support): For situations where the anchor is missing at runtime, fallback behavior should be: 1) open docs home and 2) show a toast: "Section moved — opening Console docs home" with a link to search and a short note. Make it keyboard dismissible and screen-reader friendly.

A11yBot: Toast guidance: role="status", aria-live="polite", and include a visible close button reachable by keyboard. The landing element should receive focus programmatically.

Eleni (Product): Owners: Kendrick = anchor policy + CI linter + redirect table, Sam = anchor-manifest + console integration + deploy checks, Ravi = preview modal + offset scroll UX, Nina = support KB updates and fallback wording. Add QA ticket: 4 deep-links across top pages (desktop + mobile + SR) to validate landing, focus, and fallback.

Kendrick (Docs): I'll start adding explicit IDs to the most linked pages and publish the contributor note today. Will include canonical link samples like `https://docs.redwood.inference/console/usage#autoscaling`.

Sam (DevEx): ETA for manifest POC and CI check is by end of week. I will include a small example curl and a JSON sample: `{ "usage": ["autoscaling","rate-limits"] }`.

Ravi (Design): I'll mock the modal preview and the microcopy: "Open docs for this control (new tab)" and share screens.

Nina (Support): I'll wait for the canonical list and update canned replies. Also happy to help test the fallback flows.

Eleni (Product): Thanks all. Let's close this after the QA ticket is green.

A11yBot: Action items logged: docs-anchor-policy (Kendrick), anchor-manifest-api (Sam), preview-modal-ux (Ravi), support-kb-links (Nina), qa-deep-link-tests (Eleni).

Kendrick (Docs): Noted  opening PR for explicit IDs.
